class.name: MIDIHeader
class.brief_description: Stores decoded header information from a Standard MIDI File.
class.description:
MIDIHeader represents the header chunk of a Standard MIDI File (SMF). It stores the file format, the number of tracks, and the timing division used to interpret event delta times.
The file format determines how tracks are organized. Single-track files contain one track, while the two multi-track formats describe files containing simultaneous tracks or independent sequences.
The division_type property determines how MIDI ticks are interpreted. In ticks-per-quarter-note mode, [member division] specifies the number of ticks per quarter note. In frames-per-second mode, [member frames_per_second] and [member ticks_per_frame] describe the timing resolution, and [member division] stores their product.
Use [method parse] to decode a [MIDIChunk] containing a MIDI header. Parsing fails if the chunk is not a header chunk or does not contain the minimum six bytes required for the standard header fields.

method.name: parse
method.description:
Parses a MIDI header chunk and populates this resource with its decoded values.
Returns [code]true[/code] if the chunk is a header chunk containing at least six bytes. Returns [code]false[/code] if the chunk has an incorrect type or insufficient data.
The header contains the file format, track count, and timing division. The division field determines whether timing is expressed in ticks per quarter note or in frames per second with a specified number of ticks per frame.

members.member: The MIDI file format. Determines how tracks are organized within the file.
The number of tracks declared in the MIDI file header.
The timing division mode used to interpret MIDI event delta times. A value of [code]0[/code] indicates ticks per quarter note, while [code]1[/code] indicates frames per second.

The timing resolution. In ticks-per-quarter-note mode, this is the number of ticks per quarter note. In frames-per-second mode, this is the product of [member frames_per_second] and [member ticks_per_frame].

The frame rate used for SMPTE-based timing. Populated when [member division_type] is [code]1[/code]. The encoded negative frame-rate value is converted to a positive integer; the special SMPTE value representing approximately 29.97 frames per second is therefore represented as [code]29[/code].
The number of MIDI ticks per SMPTE frame. Used when [member division_type] is [code]1[/code].

constants.constant: Format 0: the MIDI file contains a single track.
Format 1: the MIDI file contains multiple tracks intended to play simultaneously.
Format 2: the MIDI file contains multiple independent sequences.
Timing is specified as the number of ticks per quarter note. Event timing depends on the MIDI tempo.
Timing is specified using a frame rate and a number of ticks per frame. Event timing is independent of tempo changes.
